about: How a consumer that needs 'the' yield series of a crop in a country picks one (E156). A series is never spliced from two sources: for each crop and country the consumer uses ONE source — the first in national_precedence that holds a national series for it. A consumer may also name a source explicitly. This order is the platform's stated choice, changed only here (a reviewed commit).

why.FAOSTAT QCL bulk: the longest series (1961→), one definition for every country, calendar years
why.EUROSTAT apro_cpsh1: used where FAOSTAT holds no series for the crop (durum wheat), EU-27 / EFTA / UK / candidates

never_in_history.USDA FAS PSD: market years and some definitions differ from FAO's (milled rice, oils, shelled almonds) — read only as the latest-season estimate, never spliced into a history

regional: a regional series (region_code ≠ '') is read only when a consumer names its source and region
